summary: Wolfgang Schlüter was a linguist who studied under Leo Meyer at the University of Tartu from circa 1867 to 1874. He later held a post at the University of Tartu from circa 1877 to 1914.

Wolfgang Schultz worked in philosophy and history/archaeology, earning his Ph.D. from the University of Vienna around 1900–1904. He served at the Forschungsinstitut für Osten und Orient (1918–1921) and became Professor and Chair of Philosophy at the University of Munich in 1934.

Wolfgang Voigt was an Indology and Iranian/Central Asian studies scholar who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin and the University of Marburg. He served at the Royal Library of Berlin, the Westdeutsche Bibliothek, and directed the Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project.

Wolfram Eberhard specialized in Sinology and history/archaeology, studying in Berlin under Ferdinand Lessing. He taught in China, served at Ankara University (1937–1948), and was Professor of Sociology at the University of California, Berkeley (1948–1976).

Woncheol Yun is a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD from Stony Brook University. He held an attested post as Professor of Religious Studies at Seoul National University in 2012.

Woodford Wright Sherlock was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who completed an M.A. at Trinity College Dublin in 1852. He served as Lecturer in Hindustani at University College London in 1884 and at the University of Cambridge from 1883 to 1912.

Woosung Huh specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies and earned a PhD from the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa. He served as a professor in the Department of Philosophy at Kyung Hee University, attested in 2012.
Wouter J. Hanegraaff is a religious studies scholar who studied at Utrecht University from circa 1985 to 1995. He held a post at the University of Amsterdam around 1999.
Wulstan Fletcher is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under traditional teachers Pema Wangyal Rinpoche and Jigme Khyentse Rinpoche, attested in 1999.

Władysław Kotwicz was a linguistics and Iranian/Central Asian scholar who studied at St. Petersburg University (circa 1891–1895). He held posts at Saint Petersburg State University (circa 1900–1923), the Leningrad Orient Institute (circa 1920–1923), and the University of Lviv (circa 1924–1944).
Włodzimir Szajan was an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Lviv under Stefan Bołeslaw Stasiak.
Xi Cao works in computational studies and Tibetology, holding posts at Minzu University of China and Tibet University.
Xianda is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a BA from the University of Kelaniya and a PhD from the University of Hong Kong by 2016, supervised by K. L. Dhammajoti.

Xianlin Ji was an Indology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tsinghua University and the University of Göttingen. He served as professor, vice president, and Life Professor at Peking University, and held posts at the Chinese Academy of Sciences.

Xiaoling Wu was a Sinology and Indology scholar. He held posts at Visva-Bharati University (circa 1942–1946), Peking University (circa 1946–1953), Academia Sinica (circa 1953–1977), and the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (circa 1977–1995).
Xiaoming Hou works in Buddhist studies and Sinology, having studied as a doctoral student and held a post as a postdoctoral researcher at Ghent University, attested in 2026.

Xiaoting Wei works in Sinology and Buddhist studies. After earning an MA under Cheng Mei Ku at the National University of Singapore (attested 2004), Wei served as an Associate Lecturer at the Australian National University in 2016.

Xin Huang is a linguist and Tibetologist who studied at Sichuan Normal University and Sichuan University. Huang has held professor posts at Sichuan Minzu College (2012–2016), Sichuan Normal University (2016–2019), and Nanning Normal University (2023).

Xinchuan Huang was an Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy scholar who studied at Peking University from circa 1954 to 1958. He worked as a researcher at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences from circa 1977 to 1998.

Xinguang Ma works in religious studies, history/archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Ma studied at Northwest University and holds a post in the School of Chinese Language and Literature at Shanxi Normal University.
